mike_support: FYI — ACME (acct 3412) reporting SSE stream truncation mid-response when user switches from WiFi -> corp VPN. They see partial JSON object, client reconnects and then sometimes gets duplicate tokens/chunks. Billing shows partial tokens billed. Repro steps and logs below.

jess_cs: Acked. Can you paste repro steps + request_id? I also flagged for priority.

ticket-bot: :ticket: Created support ticket #51823 for this thread — https://redwood-support.example/51823

mike_support: Repro steps from the customer (straight from their app):
1) Start streaming completion via mobile app (iOS 16.5).
2) While stream is active, toggle VPN on (company VPN) which forces IP/route change.
3) Client sees sudden end-of-stream, partial JSON body (last chunk truncated), client reconnects and requests resume. Sometimes the server returns overlapping tokens leading to duplicates.

Minimal curl to reproduce (they used a mobile client but this is equivalent):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-4" \
  --no-buffer
```
Logs they attached (sanitized):
```
[2024-06-08T14:12:03Z] req=req_0b7a3f stream_chunk=45 sent_tokens=178
[2024-06-08T14:12:06Z] WARN connection reset by peer (client IP changed from 10.1.2.3 -> 172.16.0.45)
[2024-06-08T14:12:06Z] req=req_0b7a3f stream_chunk=45 partial_chunk=true
[2024-06-08T14:12:06Z] req=req_0b7a3f connection closed by client, initiating reconnect flow
```

oliver_runtime: Thanks, this looks like a classic NAT/pinhole rebind + client reconnection ordering issue. A couple quick notes:
- Server-side SSE sends are chunk-delimited (data: lines). If a TCP RST/FIN occurs mid-chunk the client can receive a truncated JSON if it treats last event as complete rather than waiting for full object.
- Check whether the ingress or proxy is emitting a FIN on IP change. Also check server heartbeat interval (our default = 20s) vs client reconnect backoff. If client-side reconnection retries immediately and the server has partially buffered output, client may request resume and the server can replay overlapping tokens.

Oliver asks: can you grab the full request_id (req_0b7a3f) with backend pod id and proxy id from logs? need to correlate with conn-id on the node.

mike_support: Pasting the extended log line they gave: 
```
[2024-06-08T14:12:06Z] req=req_0b7a3f pod=redwood-runtime-12 conn=conn-7f9a0a proxy=ingress-eu-3 status=RST reason="client-ip-change"
```
Also customer reported UA: "ACMEApp/4.2 (iPhone; iOS 16.5)" and they said it reproduces ~7/10 when toggling VPN.

nina_infra: Two things to try (infra side + customer guidance):
1) Infra: enable TCP keepalive and lower the server SSE heartbeat to 15s for the tenant to reduce window where partial chunks are treated as final. Also check proxy idle timeouts — increase `proxy_read_timeout` to avoid the proxy tearing the connection early on route change.
2) Customer: ask them to implement a short client-side buffer/reassembly so partial events are not parsed until a complete JSON object is received, or use `Last-Event-ID` resume semantics if they support it. If their client reconnects and immediately requests resume, add an idempotency check on server to dedupe overlapping tokens.

nina_infra: From infra logs the pod saw conn=conn-7f9a0a go RST at the same second as IP change — so NAT rebind is likely. We should treat this as a networking event, not purely runtime.

sarah_product: Quick billing Q — if a stream terminates mid-chunk and the client reconnects and receives overlapping tokens, do we credit the customer for duplicates / partial tokens?

jess_cs: Good question. I'll spin up a billing escalation. For now I'll ask ops to capture the exact token counts for req_0b7a3f and attach to ticket #51823. (Opening billing case B-2772).

mike_support: Next steps for the support ticket: I will ask the customer for a pcap of the switch, exact request_id, and to repro with heartbeat=15s. I'll attach the pod/proxy logs to the ticket and tag @oliver_runtime and @nina_infra.

jess_cs: Thanks — please include whether they can test with a WebSocket fallback (if possible) — that will help isolate if it's an HTTP proxy issue vs client behavior.

mike_support: Will do. cc @oliver_runtime @nina_infra :thumbsup:

ticket-bot: Attached logs and created billing case B-2772 to ticket #51823.

mike_support: Closing loop here once customer confirms repro with heartbeat tweak. If infra wants to try a tenant-scoped heartbeat change we can do a short window experiment.
